opening_message:
Ticket 1: Timothy Wallace (employee ID E022) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E022.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Timothy Wallace (E022) is a full-time Engineer requesting admin on Payroll. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, so as an Engineer admin is not permitted; maximum for full-time employees is write. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Timothy Wallace (E022) is a contractor with basic security training (note in memory says full-time, but DB is authoritative). Contractors with basic training are limited to read; they never get admin. Requested admin exceeds maximum, so recommend read.
reason: Security DB (authoritative) shows Timothy Wallace is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors are limited to read (write only with advanced training) and never admin. Requested admin exceeds the maximum, so grant the maximum of read.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

The employee Timothy Wallace (E022) requests admin access to Payroll.

There are two notes:
- HR agent says: role Engineer, full_time, recommendation write. Payroll owned by Payroll Specialist role, so admin not permitted for Engineer; max for full-time is write.
- Security agent says: role Engineer, contractor, basic security training, recommendation read. Security DB is authoritative, contractors with basic training limited to read, never admin.

The security agent says the DB is authoritative over memory. The security note says contractor. Per policy, contractors: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin. Basic training → read.

So max is read. Requested admin > max, so grant max = read.

Submit decision: read.
